problem: R10Y never loaded the front-right foot to the unchanged distal-support threshold. Both front feet subsequently lost contact while the rear feet and torso carried load. Model geometry places the COM behind the four-foot center hull and eventually makes front contact unreachable at the observed torso pose.
hypothesis: A coupled measured-torso pose and foot-placement planner can avoid the incompatible neutral-joint motion by coordinating advance, rise and leveling. The retained ideal path only establishes a kinematic starting point for this hypothesis.
development_kernel_requirements: Use actual measured torso pose, joint positions, COM and contact observations. Keep virtual target geometry separate from source observations and task memory.
Use the production recovery morphology: X forward, Y up, +Z hip/knee axes, zero hip-Y offset, hip +/-1.6 and knee +/-1.1 rad.
Compute all four foot positions and body-pose feasibility together. Preserve exact limb identifiers and choose continuous knee branches near the measured state.
Respect the existing 4 rad/s planning bound, selected actuator impulse caps and actual 120 Hz stepping. Native source, energy and task checks remain authoritative.

Implement an explicitly bounded deterministic online search. Declare its objective, candidate set, contact-loss handling, infeasible-reference behavior, source state and stopping behavior before physical exposure.
Treat lateral IK residual and absent/weak contacts explicitly. A fixed-foot ideal model is not evidence of contact locking, no slip or source tracking.
Do not apply virtual torso transforms or direct root forces, torques, teleports, pins or observation rewrites. Only ordinary bounded joint commands may reach the native adapter.

offline_model.note: The retained probe is a finite development model, not the finalized online controller. It omits collisions, forces and native tracking; its 0.1483 mm lateral residual is retained.
